baseline.name: Build normalized intermediate email/phone buffers
baseline.approach: Copy/lowercase the full email or collect all phone digits before constructing the mask.
baseline.space: O(n) intermediate storage plus the output

archived.name: Single scan with a four-digit rolling phone buffer
archived.time: O(n), where n is input length
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary scan state plus O(n) returned storage for email (bounded mask storage for a phone)

why: The archive retains only the phone suffix needed by the output, and reads email characters directly when producing its result.
quantitative_comparison: For a d-digit phone, the archive retains four digit characters instead of a d-character normalized digit buffer. Both still scan the input and construct the mask in linear work; with the bounded 10..13-digit phone contract this is a small storage trade-off, not a benchmarked speed gain.
tradeoffs: Rolling the four digits performs several assignments per digit. Valid ASCII email/phone formats and unchecked allocations remain assumptions; masking is not a general anonymization guarantee.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
